title: 竹田の子守唄 (Takeda no Komoriuta — Takeda Lullaby)
description: A haunting lullaby from Kyoto's Takeda district, sung by nursemaids (守り子 morikko) — young girls from poor families hired to care for wealthier households' children. The lyrics speak of longing for home, exhaustion, and hardship: 'Even if Obon comes, what is there to be happy about? No summer kimono, no sash.' The word 在所 (zaishō, hometown) and かたびら (hemp summer kimono) are characteristic Kyoto dialect. The song is a rare direct record of child labor in Edo–Meiji Japan.
